subtype: Wanting privacy but still needing comfort [Actor]
passage: Last winter I, Harsha, started closing my bedroom door. Not slamming, just closing. I had a notebook with a lock where I drew comics, and I didn't want Amma reading them. When she knocked, I said, "Wait!" and pushed it under my pillow. My big sister Gargi told everyone her little brother was getting "too grown-up." Then in February I got a high fever. I felt tiny and hot and scared, and I called for Amma three times in the night. She sat on my bed with a wet cloth, and I held the end of her sari like when I was little. Nobody mentioned the notebook. When I got better, I closed the door again. But now I leave it open a crack.

qa.q: What did Harsha keep in the notebook with a lock?
qa.a: The comics he drew.

qa.q: Why did Harsha call for Amma three times during the fever?
qa.a: He felt tiny, hot and scared, and wanted her close for comfort, even though he wanted privacy at other times.

qa.q: What did Amma do well when she sat with Harsha?
qa.a: She comforted him and didn't bring up the notebook, respecting his privacy while still being there.

qa.q: How might Amma feel seeing the door left open a crack?
qa.a: She may feel glad he still wants her near, even as he keeps some things to himself.

grounding: A boy starts closing his door and keeping a private notebook, yet wants his mother close when he is ill.

subtype: Wanting privacy but still needing comfort [Actor]
passage:
From Lalit's notebook, for Santosh's mother, who is on night shift this week.
Santosh (9) has asked me to knock before coming into his room now. I said okay, and I have. He has a shoebox under the bed marked PRIVATE, and I haven't opened it. Tonight he came out in his pyjamas, eyes red, because his team lost the school final today. He didn't want to talk. He just sat against me on the sofa until he fell asleep, and I carried him to bed. Next: I'll keep knocking, and I'll leave the sofa spot free after dinner in case he wants it again.

qa.q: What has Santosh asked Lalit to do before coming into his room?
qa.a: To knock.

qa.q: Why did Santosh sit against Lalit without talking?
qa.a: He was upset about losing the school final and wanted comfort and closeness, even if not words.

qa.q: Why is leaving the sofa spot free after dinner a good idea?
qa.a: It offers comfort without pushing, so Santosh can come close when he needs to while keeping his privacy.

qa.q: How might Lalit have felt when Santosh sat close on the sofa until falling asleep?
qa.a: Lalit may have felt tender and relieved that Santosh still came for comfort, which is why Lalit plans to leave the sofa spot free after dinner.

grounding: An adult at home respects a boy's new wish for privacy and is there when the boy needs comfort after a loss.

subtype: Wanting privacy but still needing comfort [Actor]
passage:
Saturday
Put a sign on my door: KNOCK FIRST. Mummy laughed, but she knocks now. Gurleen didi doesn't, so I made the sign bigger. Papa says his boy has become very secret.
I do have secrets now. Like I got 6 out of 10 in the spelling test and hid it in my geography book. Also I have a best friend at school and we have a code.
But today I fell off my cycle near the park and my knee was bleeding a lot. I didn't want to be brave. I wanted Mummy. She cleaned it, sat with me and made haldi milk. I let her stay in my room without knocking.
Tomorrow the sign goes back up.
Kishore

qa.q: What did Kishore write on the sign?
qa.a: KNOCK FIRST.

qa.q: What did Kishore want when the knee was bleeding?
qa.a: He didn't want to be brave; he wanted Mummy close to comfort him.

qa.q: Which of Mummy's choices helped Kishore feel both safe and respected?
qa.a: She knocks when he asks, yet came to clean his knee and sit with him when he needed her.

qa.q: How might Gurleen didi feel about the bigger sign?
qa.a: She might find it funny or feel a bit shut out, but it shows her brother wants some space of his own now 🙂

grounding: A boy puts a knock-first sign on his door and keeps small secrets, yet wants his mother close when he is hurt.

subtype: Wanting privacy but still needing comfort [Actor]
passage:
In their house at the edge of the mustard fields, Neelam, ten, had hung an old dupatta across the doorway of the small back room and called it her room. Under the cot she kept a tin box with ribbons, a friend's letter and a drawing she showed no one. "Knock first, Ammi," she said, though there was no door. Dilnaz tapped the wall and smiled.
On Thursday, Neelam's friend Rubina told everyone at the handpump that Neelam still sucked her thumb at night. Neelam walked home fast and climbed straight into Ammi's lap in the kitchen, face in her shoulder, too old for it and not caring.
Dilnaz only stroked her hair. Later Neelam went back behind the dupatta, but she left it half open.

qa.q: What did Neelam hang across the doorway?
qa.a: An old dupatta.

qa.q: Why did Neelam climb into Ammi's lap even though she felt too old for it?
qa.a: She was hurt and embarrassed after Rubina's teasing, and needed comfort more than privacy just then.

qa.q: What did Dilnaz's quiet response get right?
qa.a: By stroking her hair without questions, she gave comfort without prying, respecting Neelam's growing privacy.

qa.q: What might the half-open dupatta tell Dilnaz?
qa.a: That Neelam still wants her own space but also wants Ammi close, so both needs are there at once.

grounding: A ten-year-old makes a private corner and keeps secrets, yet runs to her mother's lap when upset, showing autonomy growing alongside attachment.

subtype: Wanting privacy but still needing comfort [Actor]
passage:
For her tenth birthday in Lagos, Ada got a diary with a tiny brass lock and wore the key on a string around her neck. When her mum, Esther, came in to put away laundry, Ada slammed the diary shut. "Mum! Private." She also asked Esther to stop reading her messages on the family tablet.
Esther said, "Fair enough," and started knocking.
Two nights later a storm rattled the windows and the power went out. Ada lay listening to the thunder. At midnight she padded down the dark corridor and stood at her mother's door. "Can you sit with me? Just till I sleep."
Esther sat on the edge of Ada's bed, the diary key clinking on its string as Ada turned over, and stayed until her breathing slowed.

qa.q: Where did Ada wear the diary key?
qa.a: On a string around her neck.

qa.q: What was Ada feeling when she stood at her mother's door at midnight?
qa.a: She was frightened by the storm and wanted comfort, even though she had been guarding her privacy.

qa.q: Which of Esther's choices helped Ada feel both independent and safe?
qa.a: Agreeing to knock and respect the diary, and then sitting with her through the storm without any comment about privacy.

qa.q: How might Esther see Ada's midnight request after days of 'Private'?
qa.a: She may feel reassured that Ada still needs her, even as she makes room for Ada's secrets.

grounding: A ten-year-old guards a locked diary and asks for privacy, yet wants her mother close during a frightening storm.
